To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of hepatitis C infection in children in the USA is increasing, and that the majority of infected children are infected by vertical transmission, and that the prevalence of HCV infection is higher among children born to mothers with HCV infection who were not treated for their HCV during pregnancy, compared to those mothers who were treated for HCV during pregnancy.

• HCV infection is a serious public health problem, with an estimated 3–4 million children infected worldwide; • The majority of children with HCV are infected perinatally; • HCV is a leading cause of chronic liver disease and liver-related morbidity and mortality in children and young adults; and • The optimal management of pediatric HCV infection remains unclear, and further studies are needed.
